## File: README.md

<div align="center">

<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mgpl-diagnostics/report-kit/main/assets/report-assets/logo.svg" alt="MGPL Diagnostics" width="300" />

# api

**The MGPL Diagnostics backend: one GraphQL endpoint for the whole lab.**

Sign-in, patients, bookings, samples, results, reports, billing, books, GST, receivables, settlements,
cash and bank, documents. TypeScript, GraphQL Yoga on Fastify, PostgreSQL or MongoDB.

[![Endpoint](https://img.shields.io/badge/endpoint-POST%20%2Fgraphql-14264A)](#)
[![Databases](https://img.shields.io/badge/db-PostgreSQL%20%7C%20MongoDB-14264A)](#)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-All%20rights%20reserved-E9A23B)](LICENSE)

[Docs](docs/README.md) · [Architecture](docs/02-architecture.md) · [Getting started](docs/03-getting-started.md) · [API reference](docs/04-api-reference.md) · [Client](docs/14-client.md)

</div>

---

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  APP["Apps<br/>@mgpl-diagnostics/client"] -- "POST /graphql" --> API["api<br/>controllers → services"]
  API --> K["auth-kit · db-kit · catalog-kit<br/>report-kit · invoice-kit · tally-kit · finance-kit"]
  K --> DB[("PostgreSQL / MongoDB")]
  K -.-> R[("Redis")]
  R -. "BullMQ jobs" .-> W["worker<br/>emails · documents"]
  W --> K
```

## What you get

- **One endpoint.** 140 queries and mutations; reports and invoices come back as base64 PDFs or HTML
  inside the response, CSV exports as text. No other routes except `GET /health`.
- **The kits as internal libraries.** auth-kit sessions and roles, db-kit storage and workflows,
  catalog-kit prices and reference ranges, report-kit and invoice-kit rendering, tally-kit books,
  finance-kit GST and finance. See [docs/01-overview.md](docs/01-overview.md).
- **Access and refresh tokens.** Short-lived JWTs plus single-use, rotating refresh tokens bound to the
  device; logout and disabling still apply at once. See [docs/06](docs/06-auth-and-permissions.md).
- **A worker on Redis + BullMQ** for reset emails and background documents (`npm run worker`); without
  Redis the same jobs run in the API process. See [docs/16-worker.md](docs/16-worker.md).
- **Layers.** `schema/` (SDL) → `controllers/` (permissions, mapping) → `services/` (kit calls) → kits.
- **Safe by construction.** The organisation and user come from the session; every record is checked
  against them and against its branch; unknown errors are masked; depth and list limits.
- **Money in paise, books always balanced.** Every invoice, payment and credit note posts its voucher in
  the same transaction.

## Quick start

```bash
npm run kits                       # build + install the kits (see docs/03-getting-started.md)
cp .env.example .env               # DATABASE_URL, …
SEED_ORG_NAME=… SEED_ORG_CODE=MGPL SEED_BRANCH_CODE=ARG01 SEED_BRANCH_NAME=Arang SEED_BRANCH_STATE=22 \
SEED_OWNER_NAME=… SEED_OWNER_EMAIL=… SEED_OWNER_PASSWORD=… npm run seed
npm run dev                        # http://localhost:4000/graphql
```

```graphql
mutation { login(input: { email: "owner@example.in", password: "…", orgCode: "MGPL" }) { token } }

query { viewer { user { name } organization { name } permissions } }
```

```ts
import { createMgplGraphQLClient } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/client";
const mgpl = createMgplGraphQLClient({ url: "http://localhost:4000/graphql" });
await mgpl.auth.login({ email, password, orgCode: "MGPL" });
const hits = await mgpl.catalog.search("cbc");
```

## Docs

Everything from A to Z is in [docs/](docs/README.md), with Mermaid diagrams: overview, architecture,
getting started, the generated API reference, errors, auth and permissions, domain flows, documents,

[examples](docs/examples/). What has to happen outside this repo (releases, org settings, deployment) is
in [docs/LOCAL-AGENT-BRIEF.md](docs/LOCAL-AGENT-BRIEF.md).

## Development

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test                    # end-to-end over HTTP on PostgreSQL + MongoDB (TEST_BACKENDS=pg for one)
npm run build               # dist/main.js, dist/index.js
npm run schema              # schema.graphql
npm run docs:reference      # docs/04-api-reference.md
npm run llms                # llms-full.txt
```

## File: AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md — @mgpl-diagnostics/api

The MGPL Diagnostics backend: **one GraphQL endpoint** (`POST /graphql`, GraphQL Yoga on Fastify) over
the kits, used as internal libraries. Read [docs/README.md](docs/README.md) for the full picture and
[docs/13-adding-a-feature.md](docs/13-adding-a-feature.md) before adding anything.

## Map

```
src/main.ts            start (config → container → server)
src/worker.ts          start the worker (config → container → BullMQ workers; needs REDIS_URL)
src/server.ts          Fastify + Yoga + GET /health (no other routes); security-kit headers and client IP
src/container.ts       createDb (posting: financePosting) + createAuth (JWT) + job queue + services, once per process
src/jobs/              queues (BullMQ or in-process), job payloads, processors, webhook mailer
src/config/env.ts      loadConfig: every environment variable
src/graphql/           schema.ts (MODULES → buildSchema), context, guards, errors, scalars, loaders, limits, device
src/schema/            SDL per module: base auth organization catalog lab billing books finance documents
src/controllers/       resolvers per module: authorize → map → service
src/services/          business calls on the kits: (actor, input), ownership checks, no GraphQL
scripts/               kits.mjs (build kits from source), seed.ts, print-schema.ts, api-reference.ts, llms-full.mjs
test/run.ts            end-to-end over HTTP on PostgreSQL + MongoDB, plus docs/examples validation
docs/                  A-to-Z docs (Mermaid), examples/*.graphql, LOCAL-AGENT-BRIEF.md
schema.graphql         printed schema (generated)
kits.json              kit refs for `npm run kits`
```

## Rules

1. **One endpoint.** Everything is a GraphQL field. No REST routes besides `GET /health`; documents
   travel as `Document { base64 | html }`, exports as `CsvFile`.
2. **Layers.** Schema → controller → service → kit. Controllers check permissions and map; services hold
   the logic and never import GraphQL; storage changes go to db-kit, finance rules to finance-kit,
   posting to tally-kit, permissions to auth-kit, catalog data to catalog-kit, layouts to report-kit /
   invoice-kit, mail designs to mail-kit (written in its mail design language, never HTML).
3. **Tenant isolation.** No argument carries an `orgId` or `actorId`. They come from the session
   (`actorOf`). Every id is checked against the organisation (`mustOwn`, `owned`, `scopedFind`).
4. **Permissions per branch.** Load a record, then `authorize(ctx, perm, record.branchId)`; lists use
   `branchScope`. Every permission must exist in auth-kit's `PERMISSIONS`.
5. **Errors.** Wrap controllers in `withErrorCodes`. Never build a `GraphQLError` with `originalError`
   (Yoga masks it). Error codes are a public contract: add, never rename.
6. **Money is integer paise; days are IST `Day` strings; the financial year is April–March.**
7. **No N+1.** Nested fields go through `ctx.loaders`. Lists are capped with `cap()` (≤ 200).
8. **Both databases.** Tests run on PostgreSQL and MongoDB; a change must pass on both.
9. **Generated files stay current** (CI checks): `npm run schema`, `npm run docs:reference`, `npm run llms`.
10. **Client contract.** `@mgpl-diagnostics/client` mirrors the schema; when a field is added or renamed,
    update the client (operations, types, method, docs) and bump its ref in `kits.json`.
11. **Compliance values are configuration** verified by the lab's CA (`verifyWithCA`). Ask the owner
    before changing one. No doctor referral commissions.
12. **Jobs.** Permissions are checked before a job is queued; processors call services (never GraphQL);
    job payloads carry ids and the actor, never tokens or secrets. Every job runs both on BullMQ and in-process.
13. **Tokens.** Access tokens are auth-kit JWTs; refresh tokens and device binding live in auth-kit. Device
    signals are collected by security-kit in the client; `src/graphql/device.ts` maps DeviceInput to auth-kit.
    Security headers and the client IP come from security-kit's `fastifySecurity` (never Fastify's own
    `req.ip` with a trust-all proxy setting: the left X-Forwarded-For entry is client-controlled).
14. Never commit patient data, signatures, secrets or `.env` files. Test fixtures use fictional names.

## Commands

```bash
npm run kits                       # once, and after changing kits.json
npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build
npm run schema && npm run docs:reference && npm run llms
```

`npm test` downloads PostgreSQL and MongoDB binaries on first run. Behind a proxy that blocks MongoDB,
set `MONGOMS_SYSTEM_BINARY` or run `TEST_BACKENDS=pg npm test` (CI still runs both).

## Repository rules

`main` takes pull requests only: squash merge, 1 code-owner review (`@BackStacked`), the `ci` check
required. Rules come from `mgpl-diagnostics/.github` (`scripts/protect-repos.mjs`).

## Licence

All rights reserved (see LICENSE).

## File: docs/01-overview.md

# 01 · Overview

`@mgpl-diagnostics/api` is the backend of MGPL Diagnostics (Maa Gayatri Path Lab). It serves **everything
through one endpoint, `POST /graphql`**: sign-in and users, the test catalog, patients, bookings, samples,
results and reports, billing, the books of account, GST returns, B2B receivables, partner settlements,
cash and bank, lock dates, CSV exports, and the rendered report and invoice documents.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Frontends
    W["Web app"]
    M["Mobile / desk app"]
    S["Scripts"]
  end
  W & M & S -- "POST /graphql<br/>Bearer token" --> API["api<br/>GraphQL Yoga on Fastify"]
  API --> PG[("PostgreSQL<br/>or MongoDB")]
  API -.-> R[("Redis<br/>optional")]
  LB["Load balancer"] -- "GET /health" --> API
```

## What it is made of

The domain logic lives in the kits, which the API uses as **internal libraries**. It has no other HTTP
routes and starts no per-kit servers. The kits never see HTTP: the API calls their functions from its
service layer.

| Kit | Role inside the API |
|---|---|
| [auth-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/auth-kit) | Passwords (scrypt), sessions, login rate limits, roles and permissions |
| [db-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/db-kit) | Repositories on PostgreSQL or MongoDB, transactions, workflows (bookings, reports, invoices) |
| [catalog-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/catalog-kit) | The test catalog: names, codes, prices, units, reference ranges, search |
| [report-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/report-kit) | Report PDFs and HTML (Navy Sidebar and classic designs) |
| [invoice-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/invoice-kit) | Invoice PDFs and HTML, invoice arithmetic |
| [tally-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/tally-kit) | Our own double-entry engine: ledgers, vouchers, books reports |
| [finance-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/finance-kit) | GST, GSTR-1/3B data, receivables, settlements, cash and bank, lock dates, exports |
| [security-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/security-kit) | Security headers on every response, the client IP behind proxies (`TRUST_PROXY`); in the client, the device signals |
| [client](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/client) | Not used by the API; the frontend SDK that calls it |

## Design choices

- **One endpoint.** Reports and invoices are GraphQL fields too. A PDF arrives as base64 inside the
  response (`Document.base64`), HTML as a string, CSV exports as `CsvFile.content`.
- **Layers.** Schema (SDL) → controllers (resolvers: permissions, mapping) → services (business calls on
  the kits) → kits → database. See [02-architecture.md](02-architecture.md).
- **Tenant isolation by construction.** The organisation and the acting user come from the session,
  never from arguments. Every id is checked against the session's organisation.
- **Money in integer paise**, days as IST `"YYYY-MM-DD"`, the Indian financial year (April–March).
- **Both databases.** The same code runs on PostgreSQL (Sequelize) or MongoDB (Mongoose, replica set).

## What it is not

- Not a public API for patients. Every operation except `health`, `login`, password reset and the
  catalog needs a staff session.
- Not tax advice. GST rates, TDS and thresholds are configuration that the lab's CA must confirm
  (`verifyWithCA` lists them).
- Not integrated with Tally software. tally-kit is our own engine with Tally-like concepts.


---

## File: docs/02-architecture.md

# 02 · Architecture

## Layers

Each layer talks only to the one below it. Controllers never touch the database directly except through
the per-request loaders; services never see GraphQL.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph HTTP["HTTP · src/server.ts"]
    F["Fastify<br/>POST /graphql · GET /health"]
    Y["GraphQL Yoga<br/>CORS · masked errors · depth limit 12 · introspection switch"]
  end
  subgraph GQL["GraphQL · src/graphql + src/schema"]
    SDL["SDL per module<br/>src/schema/*.graphql.ts"]
    CTX["Request context<br/>viewer · can() · loaders"]
  end
  subgraph CTRL["Controllers · src/controllers"]
    C["Resolvers<br/>authorize() · map enums · call services"]
  end
  subgraph SRV["Services · src/services"]
    S["Business calls<br/>(actor, input) → kits"]
  end
  subgraph KITS["Kits (internal libraries)"]
    K1["auth-kit"]
    K2["db-kit"]
    K3["catalog-kit"]
    K4["report-kit · invoice-kit"]
    K5["tally-kit · finance-kit"]
  end
  DB[("PostgreSQL / MongoDB")]
  RD[("Redis (optional)")]
  subgraph JOBS["Jobs · src/jobs"]
    Q["JobQueue<br/>BullMQ on Redis, or in-process"]
    W["Worker · src/worker.ts<br/>processors → the same services"]
  end
  F --> Y --> SDL --> C
  Y --> CTX --> C
  C --> S --> KITS
  S --> Q
  Q -.-> RD
  RD -.-> W
  W --> S
  K2 --> DB
  K1 -.-> RD
  K2 -.-> RD
```

| Layer | Folder | Does | Does not |
|---|---|---|---|
| Server | `src/server.ts`, `src/main.ts` | Fastify, Yoga, `/health`, shutdown | Business logic |
| Worker | `src/worker.ts` | BullMQ workers on Redis, shutdown | HTTP |
| Jobs | `src/jobs/` | Queue (BullMQ or in-process), job payloads, processors that call services, the webhook mailer | Permissions (checked before queueing) |
| Schema | `src/schema/` | SDL, one file per module | Code |
| GraphQL plumbing | `src/graphql/` | Context, guards, errors, scalars, loaders, limits, schema assembly | Domain rules |
| Controllers | `src/controllers/` | Permissions, argument mapping, nested fields | Database writes |
| Services | `src/services/` | Calls into the kits with `(actor, input)`, transactions, ownership checks | GraphQL types or errors |
| Container | `src/container.ts` | Builds db, auth and services once per process | Per-request state |
| Config | `src/config/env.ts` | Reads and checks environment variables | Defaults that are unsafe in production |

## Folders

```
src/
  main.ts               start: loadConfig → createContainer → buildServer → listen; SIGINT/SIGTERM close
  worker.ts             start the worker: loadConfig → createContainer → startWorkers (needs REDIS_URL)
  server.ts             Fastify + Yoga (one endpoint) + GET /health
  container.ts          createDb (posting: financePosting), createAuth (JWT mode; Redis or memory stores), job queue, services
  index.ts              library entry (buildServer, createContainer, buildSchema, … for tests and embedding)
  config/env.ts         loadConfig(env) → Config
  graphql/
    schema.ts           MODULES (typeDefs + resolvers per module) → buildSchema()
    context.ts          RequestContext, createContext (bearer token → auth-kit context)
    guards.ts           actorOf, authorize, canSee, branchScope, cap
    errors.ts           ERROR_CODES, toGraphQLError, withErrorCodes
    scalars.ts          DateTime, Day, JSON
    loaders.ts          per-request BatchLoader per entity (no N+1)
    limits.ts           depthLimit
    device.ts           DeviceInput (collected by security-kit in the client) → auth-kit DeviceSignals
  jobs/
    types.ts            QUEUES, job payloads, JobInfo, JobQueue, JobFailure
    processors.ts       password-reset, document rendering (call services)
    bullmq.ts           createBullJobQueue (producer), startWorkers (consumer)
    inline.ts           createInlineJobQueue (no Redis: runs at once in this process)
    mailer.ts           mailerFromConfig: mail-kit over SMTP_URL (mailKitMailer), else webhookMailer (MAIL_WEBHOOK_URL)
  schema/<module>.graphql.ts      SDL
  controllers/<module>.controller.ts
  services/<area>.service.ts, index.ts (createServices), util.ts
scripts/                kits.mjs, seed.ts, print-schema.ts, api-reference.ts, llms-full.mjs
test/run.ts             end-to-end suite over HTTP (app.inject)
schema.graphql          the printed schema (CI checks it is current)
kits.json               which kit versions CI builds (see 11-testing.md)
```

Modules: `base`, `auth`, `organization`, `catalog`, `lab`, `billing`, `books`, `finance`, `documents`.

## A request, end to end

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Cl as Client
  participant Fa as Fastify
  participant Yo as Yoga
  participant Cx as createContext
  participant Au as auth-kit
  participant Ct as Controller
  participant Sv as Service
  participant Kt as db-kit / finance-kit
  participant DB as Database
  Cl->>Fa: POST /graphql (Authorization: Bearer access JWT)
  Fa->>Yo: handleNodeRequestAndResponse
  Yo->>Yo: parse, validate (depth ≤ 12, introspection rule)
  Yo->>Cx: build context
  Cx->>Au: context(t) → verifies the JWT, checks the session, re-reads the user
  Au-->>Cx: viewer, can(), branchesFor()
  Yo->>Ct: resolve issueInvoice(input)
  Ct->>Ct: authorize(ctx, "invoice:create", input.branchId)
  Ct->>Sv: billing.issue(actor, input)
  Sv->>Kt: issueInvoice(repos, …) inside repos.transaction()
  Kt->>DB: invoice + voucher (posting hook) atomically
  DB-->>Kt: ok
  Kt-->>Sv: Invoice
  Sv-->>Ct: Invoice
  Ct-->>Yo: Invoice (nested fields via loaders)
  Yo-->>Cl: { data: { issueInvoice: … } }
```

If anything throws, `withErrorCodes` turns domain errors (from db-kit, auth-kit, finance-kit,
report-kit) into GraphQL errors with a code; any other error is masked as "Unexpected error"
([05-errors.md](05-errors.md)).

## How the kits depend on each other

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  API["api"] --> AUTH["auth-kit"]
  API --> DB["db-kit"]
  API --> CAT["catalog-kit"]
  API --> INV["invoice-kit"]
  API --> REP["report-kit"]
  API --> FIN["finance-kit"]
  API --> TAL["tally-kit"]
  INV --> REP
  FIN --> TAL
  FIN --> DB
  TAL --> DB
  DB -. "stores users for" .-> AUTH
  CL["client (frontend)"] -. "POST /graphql" .-> API
```

- db-kit's repositories satisfy auth-kit's store interfaces (users, orgs, roles, audit), so auth-kit reads
  and writes users through db-kit (`container.ts` passes `db.rawRepos`).
- db-kit posts billing to the books through a `PostingHook`. The API sets it to finance-kit's
  `financePosting`, which posts through tally-kit with GST split by place of supply.
- `src/graphql` in db-kit is an older, partial GraphQL layer. This API replaces it; db-kit will remove
  it in a major version ([LOCAL-AGENT-BRIEF.md](LOCAL-AGENT-BRIEF.md)).

## The container

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  ENV["process.env"] --> CFG["loadConfig()"]
  CFG --> CON["createContainer()"]
  CON --> DBX["createDb({ backend, url, redis?, posting: financePosting })"]
  CON --> AUX["createAuth({ users, orgs, roles, audit from db,<br/>sessions/kv/limiter from Redis or memory, jwt, deviceBinding })"]
  CON --> JQ["job queue: BullMQ (REDIS_URL) or in-process"]
  CON --> SVX["createServices(db.repos, auth, mailer, lab, jobs)"]
  CON -. "jobDeps" .-> WK["startWorkers (src/worker.ts)"]
  CON --> SRV["buildServer(container)"]
```

One container per process. Tests build it with an embedded database and a capturing mailer; production
builds it from the environment. `close()` closes what the container opened.

## Cross-cutting rules

1. **Tenant isolation.** Services take an `Actor { userId, orgId }` from the session. `mustOwn` / `owned`
   check that a record's `orgId` matches before anything is returned or changed.
2. **Branch scoping.** `authorize(ctx, perm, branchId)` checks the record's own branch; list queries use
   `branchScope`, which narrows to the branches where the user holds the permission.
3. **Transactions.** Multi-record writes run in `repos.transaction()` inside the kits.
4. **No N+1.** Nested fields (`Booking.patient`, `Invoice.branch`, …) go through per-request loaders.
5. **Limits.** Query depth ≤ 12, list `limit` ≤ 200, request body ≤ 2 MB by default.


---

## File: docs/03-getting-started.md

# 03 · Getting started

## Requirements

- Node.js ≥ 20 (CI uses 22)
- PostgreSQL ≥ 14, **or** MongoDB ≥ 6 running as a replica set (transactions need one)
- Redis (optional; needed when you run more than one server)
- Git (to build the kits from source until they are all on the registry)

## 1. Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/api && cd api
npm run kits          # builds the 7 kits + client from source at the refs in kits.json, then npm install
```

`npm run kits` exists because not every kit is published to GitHub Packages yet. Once they are, a plain
`npm install` (with a token that has `read:packages`) is enough; see [LOCAL-AGENT-BRIEF.md](LOCAL-AGENT-BRIEF.md).
To build from local checkouts instead of GitHub, set `KITS_SRC=/path/to/folder-with-the-kits`.

## 2. Configure

```bash
cp .env.example .env   # then edit DATABASE_URL etc.; see 09-configuration.md
```

## 3. Seed the first organisation

Once per new database. It creates the organisation, its first branch, the owner, the system roles and the
chart of accounts with finance-kit's ledgers.

```bash
SEED_ORG_NAME="Maa Gayatri Path Lab" SEED_ORG_CODE=MGPL SEED_ORG_GSTIN=22XXXXX0000X1Z5 \
SEED_BRANCH_CODE=ARG01 SEED_BRANCH_NAME=Arang SEED_BRANCH_STATE=22 \
SEED_OWNER_NAME="Lab Owner" SEED_OWNER_EMAIL=owner@example.in SEED_OWNER_PASSWORD='a long passphrase' \
npm run seed
```

- `SEED_BRANCH_STATE` is the GST state code of the branch (22 = Chhattisgarh). **Billing needs it**: the
  posting hook decides CGST+SGST vs IGST from it.
- `SEED_ORG_GSTIN` is optional for billing but **required for GSTR-1 / GSTR-3B**.
- The password must pass auth-kit's policy (length, not containing the email or name, not common).

## 4. Run

```bash
npm run dev            # tsx watch, http://localhost:4000/graphql (GraphiQL in development)
# or
npm run build && npm start
```

## 5. First calls

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant You
  participant API
  You->>API: mutation login(email, password, orgCode)
  API-->>You: token
  You->>API: query viewer (Bearer token)
  API-->>You: user, organization, permissions
  You->>API: mutation setupChartOfAccounts (idempotent)
  You->>API: query catalogSearch("cbc")
```

```bash
curl -s localhost:4000/graphql -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"mutation($i: LoginInput!){ login(input: $i){ token user { name } } }","variables":{"i":{"email":"owner@example.in","password":"…","orgCode":"MGPL"}}}'

curl -s localhost:4000/graphql -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"query":"{ viewer { user { name } organization { name branches { code stateCode } } permissions } }"}'
```

More in [examples/](examples/): a full day at the desk ([lab-day.graphql](examples/lab-day.graphql)),
billing and books ([billing-and-books.graphql](examples/billing-and-books.graphql)), finance
([finance.graphql](examples/finance.graphql)) and documents ([documents.graphql](examples/documents.graphql)).

## 6. Useful commands

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test                      # end-to-end on PostgreSQL and MongoDB (TEST_BACKENDS=pg to pick one)
npm run schema                # rewrite schema.graphql
npm run docs:reference        # rewrite docs/04-api-reference.md
npm run llms                  # rewrite llms-full.txt
```

# 04 · API reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:reference` (scripts/api-reference.ts). Do not edit by hand. -->

Every operation of `POST /graphql`, grouped by module, with the permission its resolver checks.
**Permission** lists what `authorize()` requires; a branch-scoped permission is checked against the
record's branch (see [06-auth-and-permissions.md](06-auth-and-permissions.md)). `public` means no
sign-in is needed; `(signed in)` means any signed-in user. The full SDL is [schema.graphql](../schema.graphql),
and runnable examples are in [examples/](examples/).

## base

| Kind | Operation | Permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| query | `health: Health!` | public |  |
| mutation | `ping: String!` | public | Does nothing; lets clients check that mutations reach the server. |

| Kind | Operation | Permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| query | `mySessions: [Session!]!` | (signed in) |  |
| query | `permissions: [String!]!` | (signed in) | Every permission name the API checks. |
| query | `roles: [Role!]!` | `role:read` |  |
| query | `user(id: ID!): User` | `user:read` |  |
| query | `users: [User!]!` | `user:read` |  |
| query | `viewer: Viewer` | public | null when not signed in. |
| mutation | `changePassword(currentPassword: String!, newPassword: String!): Boolean!` | (signed in) |  |
| mutation | `createUser(input: CreateUserInput!): User!` | `user:create` |  |
| mutation | `disableUser(userId: ID!): User!` | `user:disable` |  |
| mutation | `enableUser(userId: ID!): User!` | `user:disable` |  |
| mutation | `login(input: LoginInput!): LoginResult!` | public |  |
| mutation | `logout(refreshToken: String): Boolean!` | public | Ends this session: the bearer token (even an expired access token), or the refresh token when given. |
| mutation | `logoutOtherSessions: Int!` | (signed in) | Ends every other session of the signed-in user; returns how many. |
| mutation | `refreshSession(refreshToken: String!, device: DeviceInput): LoginResult!` | public | Spends a refresh token and returns a new access token and the next refresh token. A refresh token used twice ends its session (it was copied); within a few seconds (two tabs) the second use only fails. Send the same device as at login: a refresh from another device id ends the session (DEVICE_BINDING). INVALID_TOKEN when it is unknown, spent or expired: sign in again. |
| mutation | `requestPasswordReset(email: String!, orgCode: String): Boolean!` | public | Always true (never reveals whether the email exists). Queued: the worker creates the single-use token and mails the link. |

| mutation | `revokeSession(id: ID!): Boolean!` | (signed in) |  |

## File: docs/05-errors.md

# 05 · Errors

Every error in a response carries `extensions.code`. Clients switch on the code, never on the message.

```json
{ "errors": [{ "message": "Missing permission invoice:create", "path": ["issueInvoice"],
               "extensions": { "code": "FORBIDDEN", "permission": "invoice:create" } }],
  "data": null }
```

## Codes

| Code | HTTP-ish | Raised when | Client should |
|---|---|---|---|
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 | No token, expired, logged out, or the user was disabled | Send the user to sign in |
| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | The user lacks the permission (at that branch). `extensions.permission` names it | Hide the action; explain |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The id does not exist **in this organisation** (other tenants' ids look the same) | Show "not found" |
| `BAD_USER_INPUT` | 400 | Validation failed (db-kit `ValidationError`, report-kit 400s, unknown catalog codes, …) | Show the message next to the form |
| `CONFLICT` | 409 | Duplicate key, or the wrong state (e.g. release before verify, cancel a paid invoice) | Refresh and show the message |
| `PERIOD_LOCKED` | 409 | A posting date is on or before a lock date | Ask an accountant; pick another date |
| `CREDIT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 409 | A B2B invoice would exceed the customer's credit limit | Collect payment or raise the limit |
| `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` | 401 | Wrong email, organisation or password (same answer for each) | "Email or password is wrong" |
| `ACCOUNT_DISABLED` | 403 | The user is disabled | Contact an administrator |
| `INVITE_PENDING` | 403 | The user has not set a password yet | Use the reset link |
| `ORG_REQUIRED` | 400 | The email exists in more than one organisation | Ask for the organisation code |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many attempts; `extensions.retryAfterMs` says how long to wait | Wait, then retry |
| `WEAK_PASSWORD` | 400 | The new password fails the policy | Show the message |
| `INVALID_TOKEN` | 400 | A reset token is unknown, used or expired | Request a new link |
| `GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED` | 400 | The document is invalid (unknown field, depth > 12, introspection off) | Fix the query |
| `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` | 500 | Anything else. The message is masked as "Unexpected error" | Retry later; check server logs |

## How errors are made

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  T["throw in service / kit"] --> W["withErrorCodes (wraps every controller)"]
  W -->|GraphQLError| P["passed through"]
  W -->|AuthError| A["code = AuthError.code"]
  W -->|PeriodLockedError| L["PERIOD_LOCKED"]
  W -->|CreditLimitError| CL["CREDIT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED"]
  W -->|NotFound / Conflict / ValidationError| D["NOT_FOUND / CONFLICT / BAD_USER_INPUT"]
  W -->|report-kit HttpError 400| B["BAD_USER_INPUT"]
  W -->|anything else| M["re-thrown → Yoga masks it<br/>'Unexpected error'"]
```

Source: `src/graphql/errors.ts`. Two rules there matter:

1. **Never pass `originalError`** to a `GraphQLError`. Yoga masks any error that wraps a non-GraphQL
   error, which would hide the code.
2. **Unknown errors stay masked.** Stack traces and SQL never reach clients. They are logged on the server.

## Adding a code

Codes are a public contract: add new ones, never rename. Add it to `ERROR_CODES`, map the domain error in
`toGraphQLError`, document it here and in the client's `docs/graphql.md`, and add a test.


---

## File: docs/06-auth-and-permissions.md

# 06 · Auth and permissions

## Sessions: access and refresh tokens

auth-kit owns passwords and sessions (JWT mode). `login` returns two tokens:

- **access token**: an HS256 JWT `{ sub, org, sid, iat, exp, iss }`, valid 15 minutes, sent as `Authorization: Bearer`;
- **refresh token**: opaque and single-use. `refreshSession` spends it and returns a new pair.

Revocation still applies at once: every request checks that the session (`sid`) exists and re-reads
the user. No store ever holds a raw token, only `hashToken(token)` (SHA-256).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client (SDK session manager)
  participant A as API (auth controller)
  participant K as auth-kit
  participant S as Session store + kv (Redis or memory)
  participant U as Users (db-kit)
  C->>A: login(email, password, orgCode?, device)
  A->>K: login()
  K->>U: find user (unknown email still runs one scrypt verify: timing-safe)
  K->>K: rate limit per email+ip (10 per 15 min)
  K->>S: session { random id, device }, refresh:hash(R1) → id
  K-->>C: accessToken (JWT, 15 min) + R1 + user
  C->>A: any request (Bearer JWT)
  A->>K: context(JWT): verify HS256, exp, iss
  K->>S: session still there? extend idle window
  K->>U: re-read the user (disable / role changes apply at once)
  K-->>A: viewer, can(), branchesFor()
  C->>A: refreshSession(R1, device)
  K->>S: take refresh:hash(R1) (single use), compare deviceId
  K-->>C: new JWT + R2
  Note over C,K: R1 used again later → the session ends (copied token). Another deviceId → the session ends.
```

| Setting | Default | Env |
|---|---|---|
| Access-token lifetime | 15 minutes | `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_MS` |
| Signing secret(s) | random per process in development; **required** in production | `JWT_SECRET` (≥ 32 characters; comma-separated to rotate: the first signs) |
| Issuer | `mgpl-api` | `JWT_ISSUER` |
| Idle timeout (refresh token lifetime, slides) | 12 hours | `SESSION_IDLE_MS` |
| Maximum age | 30 days | `SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS` |
| Device binding | `enforce` | `DEVICE_BINDING` (`enforce`, `flag`, `off`) |
| Login attempts | 10 per 15 minutes | (auth-kit default) |

- **Rotation.** A spent refresh token presented again within 15 s (two tabs refreshing at once) is only
  refused; later, it ends the session and is audited (`auth.refresh_reuse`).
- **Logout.** `logout` ends the bearer's session, or the session of `logout(refreshToken)` (works with an
  expired access token).
- **Rotating the secret.** Set `JWT_SECRET=new,old`, deploy, wait 15 minutes, then set `JWT_SECRET=new`.

Session operations: `mySessions` (with `deviceId` and `deviceInfo`), `revokeSession`, `logout`, `logoutOtherSessions`.

### Device signals

The client sends `device: DeviceInput` with `login` and `refreshSession`. The SDK collects these values;
any client may send them.

| Field | What it is | Server use |
|---|---|---|
| `deviceId` | random id kept by the client per browser profile or install | stored at login; a refresh from another `deviceId` → `INVALID_TOKEN`, the session ends, audit `auth.device_mismatch` (`DEVICE_BINDING=flag` only audits) |
| `fingerprint` | client-side SHA-256 of coarse device attributes (security-kit) | a change is audited (`auth.fingerprint_changed`), never blocked |
| `clientSessionId` | random id per tab or app run | stored (latest) |
| `info` | os, browser, major browser version, mobile, language, timezone, screen (client 1.3.0+; older clients sent platform, cores, memory, touch points and the user agent) | stored (latest), shown in `mySessions.deviceInfo` |

Values are untrusted: auth-kit's `cleanDeviceSignals` keeps ids of 8–128 safe characters and at most
20 short `info` values. A session that signed in without a `deviceId` is bound by its first refresh that
sends one. The client collects the signals with [security-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/security-kit); `src/graphql/device.ts` maps them to auth-kit. `changePassword`
ends the user's other sessions; `resetPassword`, an administrator's `setUserPassword` and `disableUser`
end all of them.

### Password reset

`requestPasswordReset(email, orgCode?)` always returns `true`, whether or not the account exists, and
only queues a job. The worker ([16-worker.md](16-worker.md)), or the API itself without Redis, creates
the token and sends `PASSWORD_RESET_URL?token=…` through the `Mailer` (mail-kit over `SMTP_URL`,
`MAIL_WEBHOOK_URL`, or `createContainer({ config, mailer })`). The token is never returned by the API and never stored raw.
`resetPassword(token, newPassword)` consumes it once.

## Permissions

A permission is `resource:action`. Roles grant permissions, with wildcards (`invoice:*`, `*:read`, `*:*`).
A user holds roles **per branch** (`branchId`) or **organisation-wide** (`branchId: null`).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U["User"] -- "role: technician<br/>branch: A01" --> R1["technician"]
  U -- "role: front_desk<br/>branch: (all)" --> R2["front_desk"]
  R1 --> P1["sample:*, report:enter, …"]
  R2 --> P2["patient:create, invoice:create, …"]
  P1 --> Q{"can(perm, branchId)?"}
  P2 --> Q
```

`can(permission, branchId)` is true when a role held at that branch, or organisation-wide, grants it.
Without a branch, a role at any branch counts. `permissions` (query) lists every name the API checks;
`viewer { permissions(branchId) can(permission, branchId) branchesFor(permission) }` lets a UI hide what
the user cannot do.

### System roles (auth-kit `SYSTEM_ROLES`)

| Role | Summary |
|---|---|
| `owner` | Everything (`*:*`) |
| `admin` | Branches, users, roles, all lab and billing work, `accounts:*`, audit, settings (not `org:update`) |
| `branch_manager` | Patients, bookings, samples, billing, payments; reads reports, releases them; reads accounts |
| `front_desk` | Registers patients, books tests, issues invoices, takes payments |
| `phlebotomist` | Reads bookings, collects samples |
| `technician` | Samples, enters results |
| `pathologist` | Reports: enter, verify, release, amend |
| `accountant` | Payments, invoice cancellation, all `accounts:*` (books, GST, finance), audit |
| `doctor` | Reads patients and reports |

Organisations can add their own roles or override these with `upsertRole`.

### How a resolver checks

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R["resolver"] --> A{"signed in?"}
  A -- no --> U["UNAUTHENTICATED"]
  A -- yes --> B{"record has a branch?"}
  B -- yes --> C["load record (orgId checked)<br/>authorize(ctx, perm, record.branchId)"]
  B -- "no / list" --> D["branchScope(ctx, perm, branchId?)<br/>→ allowed branches"]
  C --> E{"allowed?"}
  D --> E
  E -- no --> F["FORBIDDEN"]
  E -- yes --> G["service call"]
```

- Single records are loaded first (checking `orgId`), then authorised **against their own branch**, so
  a user cannot read another branch's booking by guessing its id.
- Lists are filtered to the branches where the user holds the permission.
- Nested fields the user may not see (e.g. `Patient.invoices` without `invoice:read`) resolve to empty
  lists, not errors.
- Books, GST and finance need `accounts:read` (reports), `accounts:post` (vouchers, settlements, cash,
  bank) or `accounts:manage` (chart, tax rules, lock dates, year end).

The generated [04-api-reference.md](04-api-reference.md) lists the exact permission per operation.

## Tenant isolation

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  T["token"] --> V["viewer.orgId"]
  V --> S["service(actor = { userId, orgId })"]
  S --> O{"record.orgId == actor.orgId?"}
  O -- no --> N["NOT_FOUND (indistinguishable from missing)"]
  O -- yes --> OK["continue"]
```

No operation accepts an `orgId`. Inputs that reference other records (patient, branch, invoice, ledger,
customer, partner) are checked against the session's organisation before use.

## File: docs/07-domain-flows.md

# 07 · Domain flows

## The lab day, end to end

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  P["registerPatient"] --> B["createBooking<br/>(tests from the catalog)"]
  B --> S["samples created<br/>one per sample type"]
  B --> I["issueInvoice<br/>(bookingId, items by code)"]
  I --> V1["sales voucher posted<br/>(GST split, finance-kit)"]
  I --> PAY["recordPayment"] --> V2["receipt voucher"]
  S --> C["collectSample"] --> R["receiveSample"]
  R --> RP["createReport → saveResults<br/>(unit, range, flag from catalog)"]
  RP --> VR["verifyReport"] --> RL["releaseReport"]
  RL --> D["bookingReportDocument<br/>PDF / HTML"]
  I --> ID["invoiceDocument<br/>PDF / HTML"]
```

## Booking

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> booked: createBooking
  booked --> sample_collected: first collectSample
  booked --> in_process: receiveSample
  sample_collected --> in_process: receiveSample
  in_process --> completed: last report released
  booked --> cancelled: cancelBooking
  sample_collected --> cancelled: cancelBooking
  in_process --> cancelled: cancelBooking
  note right of cancelled: needs the booking's invoice cancelled first
```

`createBooking` accepts `tests: [{ testCode }]`; the name, price (paise) and sample type come from the
catalog unless given. One sample (with a barcode) is created per distinct sample type.

## Sample

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> pending
  pending --> collected: collectSample
  collected --> received: receiveSample
  pending --> rejected: rejectSample(reason)
  collected --> rejected: rejectSample(reason)
  received --> rejected: rejectSample(reason)
```

## Report

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> draft: createReport
  draft --> entered: saveResults
  entered --> entered: saveResults (again)
  entered --> verified: verifyReport
  verified --> released: releaseReport
  released --> amended: amendReport
  amended --> verified: verifyReport
```

`saveResults` fills `unit`, `range` (by the patient's sex) and `flag` (L / H by the reference interval) from
the catalog when the client leaves them out. `flag: NONE` means normal. Releasing the last report of a
booking marks the booking `completed`. `bookingReportDocument` prints verified or released reports only ([08-documents.md](08-documents.md)).

## Invoice and payments

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> issued: issueInvoice (nothing paid)
  [*] --> partially_paid: issueInvoice with part payment
  [*] --> paid: issueInvoice paid in full
  issued --> partially_paid: recordPayment
  partially_paid --> paid: recordPayment
  issued --> paid: recordPayment
  paid --> partially_paid: refundPayment (part)
  paid --> refunded: refundPayment (all)
  issued --> credited: issueCreditNote (whole value)
  partially_paid --> credited: issueCreditNote
  issued --> cancelled: cancelInvoice(reason)
  refunded --> cancelled: cancelInvoice(reason)
  note right of cancelled: only with nothing paid; refund first
```

- Items may be just `{ code: "CBC" }`: name and MRP come from the catalog. `applyTaxRules: true` takes
  HSN/SAC, taxability and rate from the organisation's tax rules (diagnostic services are usually exempt).
- Arithmetic (db-kit, integer paise): line gross → line discount → bill discount shared by largest
  remainder → GST → round-off to the rupee.
- Every issue, payment, refund, credit note and cancel posts a voucher **in the same transaction**
  (`financePosting` → tally-kit). A failed posting rolls the whole operation back.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant API as billing service
  participant DB as db-kit issueInvoice
  participant H as financePosting (hook)
  participant T as tally-kit postVoucher
  API->>DB: repos.transaction(tx => …)
  DB->>DB: compute totals, number MGPL/ARG01/2026-27/000123
  DB->>H: invoiceIssued(tx, invoice)
  H->>H: place of supply from branch stateCode → CGST+SGST or IGST
  H->>T: sales voucher (Dr patient/customer, Cr income, Cr output GST)
  T->>T: assertPeriodOpen (lock dates), assertBalanced
  T-->>DB: voucher
  DB-->>API: invoice (committed with its voucher)
```

## B2B receivables

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  CU["createCustomer<br/>(credit limit, days)"] --> CI["issueCustomerInvoice"]
  CI --> CS["customerStatement<br/>open items, ageing"]
  CI --> CN["issueCreditNote<br/>(lines or whole)"]
  CS --> RS["receivablesSummary"]
```

`issueCustomerInvoice` refuses with `CREDIT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` when the customer's open balance plus this
invoice exceeds the limit. Credit notes reverse tax line by line and reduce what is owed.

## Partner settlements (collection centres, franchises)

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> draft: createSettlement(partner, "2026-09")
  draft --> accrued: accrueSettlement (journal: expense / partner)
  accrued --> paid: paySettlement (payment voucher, TDS)
  draft --> cancelled: cancelSettlement
  accrued --> cancelled: cancelSettlement (reverses accrual)
  note right of paid: corrections go into the next month
```

`settlementPreview` computes the month without saving: lines per invoice from the partner's agreements
(revenue share in basis points, or fixed rates per test code), deductions, TDS (section and rate from the
partner or the finance config) and net. No doctor referral commissions: settlements are for collection
centres and franchises only.

## Cash and bank

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Cash
    CC["closeCashDay(branch, day, counted)"] --> DIFF{"book = counted?"}
    DIFF -- no --> J["journal for the difference"]
  end
  subgraph Bank
    IM["importBankStatement(csv)"] --> RC["reconcileBank<br/>auto-match, card/UPI settlements with MDR"]
    RC --> UM["bankLines(status: unmatched)"]
    UM --> MB["matchBankLine / setBankLineStatus"]
    MB --> BR["bankReconciliation (BRS)"]
  end
```

## Periods

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  [*] --> open
  open --> locked: setLockDate(upTo)
  locked --> open: setLockDate(null)
  open --> closed: closeFinancialYear("2026-27")
  note right of locked: postings on or before upTo fail with PERIOD_LOCKED
```

`closeFinancialYear` posts the closing vouchers on 31 March (income and expenses into capital) and locks
the year. Lock dates are checked inside the posting transaction, so nothing slips past them.

## Books

`setupChartOfAccounts` seeds the 28 standard groups, the default ledgers and finance-kit's ledgers
(idempotent; the seed script runs it). Reports: `trialBalance`, `ledgerStatement`, `cashBook`, `dayBook`,
`profitAndLoss`, `balanceSheet`, `outstandingReceivables`, `gstSummary`. Manual entries go through
`postVoucher` (balanced, one side per line) and `cancelVoucher`.

## File: docs/08-documents.md

# 08 · Documents (reports and invoices)

report-kit and invoice-kit render inside the API process. There is no separate document server and no
REST route: documents travel in GraphQL responses.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Stored["From stored records"]
    BR["bookingReportDocument(bookingId, reportIds?)"]
    ID["invoiceDocument(invoiceId)"]
  end
  subgraph Ad-hoc["From a request (JSON)"]
    RR["renderReport(request)"]
    RI["renderInvoice(request)"]
    IT["invoiceTotals(request)"]
  end
  LH["letterhead"]
  BR & RR --> RK["report-kit<br/>renderReportPdf / Html"]
  ID & RI --> IK["invoice-kit<br/>renderInvoicePdf / Html"]
  LH --> RK
  RK & IK --> DOC["Document<br/>{ format, fileName, mimeType, byteLength, base64 | html }"]
```

## The Document type

| Field | PDF | HTML |
|---|---|---|
| `format` | `pdf` | `html` |
| `mimeType` | `application/pdf` | `text/html; charset=utf-8` |
| `base64` | the file | null |
| `html` | null | a self-contained page (fonts and images inlined) |
| `byteLength` | size of the PDF | size of the HTML (UTF-8) |

Arguments: `format` (`pdf` default), `variant` (`header` prints the letterhead; `non_header` for
pre-printed paper, same positions otherwise), `design` (`sidebar` default, or `classic`) for reports.

In a browser: `documentBlob(doc)` from `@mgpl-diagnostics/client` gives a Blob for download, a new tab or
printing ([14-client.md](14-client.md)).

## Stored reports → print

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  B["booking + patient + doctor + samples"] --> M["map to report-kit's Report"]
  R["verified / released reports"] --> T{"every result matches a<br/>template field key or label?"}
  T -- yes --> TPL["template section (e.g. cbc, lft)<br/>with the lab's layout"]
  T -- no --> GEN["generic section<br/>Test · Result · Unit · Range"]
  TPL & GEN --> M
  M --> RK["report-kit render"]
```

The sample-collection time is the earliest `collectedAt` of the booking's samples. Draft or entered
reports never print: if any selected report is not verified or released the call fails with `CONFLICT`
(pass `reportIds` to print only the ready ones), and `NOT_FOUND` when there are none.

## Stored invoices → print

The stored invoice (paise) is mapped to invoice-kit's print shape (rupees). invoice-kit recomputes the
totals; the API checks that its total equals the stored total and refuses a mismatch (`CONFLICT`), so a
printed invoice can never disagree with the books.

## Ad-hoc rendering

`renderReport(request)` and `renderInvoice(request)` take the same JSON as report-kit's and invoice-kit's
HTTP APIs did (`ReportRequest`: patient + tests | profile | report | sample; `InvoiceRequest`:
`{ invoice }` or `{ sample }`). They are for previews (result entry with a live preview, quotes). Samples
(`documentSamples`, `invoiceSamples`, `{ sample: id }`) work only when `MGPL_SAMPLES=true`.

## In the background

Large prints can go to the worker: `startDocumentJob(input: { kind: invoice | booking_reports, … })`
returns a `Job`, and `job(id)` returns it with `document` once `state` is `completed`. See
[16-worker.md](16-worker.md).

## Signatures and branding

The lab profile is `defaultLab()` from report-kit: branding plus signatures read from
`MGPL_SIGNATURE_HEADER_FILE` / `MGPL_SIGNATURE_NONHEADER_FILE` (or `MGPL_SIGNATURE_FILE`). The files live
outside every repository. Without them a placeholder signature prints. Embedders can pass their own
`lab` to `createContainer`.

## Cost

A PDF takes tens to a few hundred milliseconds of CPU and the response is about 4/3 of the file size
(base64). Keep `BODY_LIMIT_BYTES` for requests; responses are not limited. Render on demand; cache the
result client-side if the same document is opened repeatedly.

## File: docs/09-configuration.md

# 09 · Configuration

All configuration comes from environment variables, read once by `loadConfig()` (`src/config/env.ts`).
Copy `.env.example` to `.env` for local work; never commit it.

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `NODE_ENV` | `development` | `production` turns off GraphiQL, introspection, samples and `*` CORS by default |
| `HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | |
| `PORT` | `4000` | |
| `GRAPHQL_PATH` | `/graphql` | The one endpoint |
| `DB_BACKEND` | `pg` | `pg` or `mongo` |
| `DATABASE_URL` | local default in development; **required** in production | Postgres URL, or a MongoDB URI with `replicaSet=` |
| `REDIS_URL` | empty | Sessions, refresh tokens, login limits, db-kit's read cache and the job queues (BullMQ). Required for more than one server and for the worker |
| `CORS_ORIGINS` | `*` in development, empty in production | Comma-separated origins. `*` is refused in production |
| `GRAPHIQL` | on in development | GraphiQL at the endpoint (GET) |
| `INTROSPECTION` | on in development | Off adds `NoSchemaIntrospectionCustomRule` |
| `BODY_LIMIT_BYTES` | `2000000` | Request body limit (bank CSV imports count) |
| `TRUST_PROXY` | `false` | How many proxies in front of the API append to `X-Forwarded-For`: `true` = 1 (a load balancer), `2` for CDN + load balancer. Login limits and sessions then see the client IP; entries left of the trusted proxies (which any client can send) are ignored |
| `MGPL_SAMPLES` | on in development | Demo report/invoice samples in `documents` |
| `SESSION_IDLE_MS` | `43200000` (12 h) | |
| `SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS` | `2592000000` (30 days) | |
| `PASSWORD_RESET_URL` | empty (`/reset-password`) | The page that receives `?token=` |
| `JWT_SECRET` | random per process in development; **required** in production | Signs access tokens. ≥ 32 characters; `new,old` to rotate |
| `JWT_ISSUER` | `mgpl-api` | `iss` claim, checked on every request |
| `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_MS` | `900000` (15 min) | Access-token lifetime |
| `DEVICE_BINDING` | `enforce` | Refresh from another device: `enforce` ends the session, `flag` audits, `off` ignores |
| `QUEUE_PREFIX` | `mgpl` | BullMQ key prefix ([16-worker.md](16-worker.md)) |
| `WORKER_CONCURRENCY` | `4` | Jobs per worker at once, per queue |
| `JOB_RESULT_TTL_MS` | `3600000` (1 h) | How long finished jobs and their documents stay readable |
| `SMTP_URL` | empty | Mail through mail-kit: `smtps://user:pass@host:465` (TLS) or `smtp://user:pass@host:587` (STARTTLS). Preferred over `MAIL_WEBHOOK_URL` |
| `MAIL_FROM` | — (required with `SMTP_URL` in production) | Sender, e.g. `Maa Gayatri Path Lab <no-reply@your-domain>` |
| `MAIL_WEBHOOK_URL` | empty | Email relay for reset links when `SMTP_URL` is not set: POST `{ to, subject, text }` |
| `MGPL_SIGNATURE_HEADER_FILE` | — | PNG for the header variant (outside the repo) |
| `MGPL_SIGNATURE_NONHEADER_FILE` | — | PNG for the non-header variant |
| `MGPL_SIGNATURE_FILE` | — | One file for both |

Seed-only variables (`npm run seed`): `SEED_ORG_NAME`, `SEED_ORG_CODE`, `SEED_ORG_GSTIN` (optional),
`SEED_BRANCH_CODE`, `SEED_BRANCH_NAME`, `SEED_BRANCH_STATE`, `SEED_OWNER_NAME`, `SEED_OWNER_EMAIL`,
`SEED_OWNER_PASSWORD`.

Test-only: `TEST_BACKENDS=pg,mongo` (default both), `DEBUG=1` prints resolver errors,
`MONGOMS_SYSTEM_BINARY` points mongodb-memory-server at a local `mongod`.

## Finance configuration

GST and TDS values are not environment variables. They are data in the organisation's settings
(`settings.finance`, merged over finance-kit's `DEFAULT_FINANCE_CONFIG`) and tax rules (`taxRules`,
`addTaxRule`, `seedTaxRules`). Every value the CA must confirm is listed by `verifyWithCA`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  D["finance-kit DEFAULT_FINANCE_CONFIG"] --> MRG["merged config<br/>(financeConfig query)"]
  O["organization.settings.finance"] --> MRG
  TR["taxRules (per org)"] --> GST["GST per invoice line"]
  MRG --> GST
  MRG --> TDS["TDS on settlements"]
```

## File: docs/10-data-and-money.md

# 10 · Data and money

## Money

- **Integer paise everywhere** (`totalPaise: 35400` = Rs 354.00). Inputs and outputs, no floats.
- The catalog's `mrp` and invoice-kit's print/price-list amounts are **rupees**; the API converts at the
  boundary (`pricePaise = mrp × 100`).
- Rounding is explicit: bill discounts by largest remainder, GST per line, round-off to the rupee.
- Every voucher balances (debits = credits), checked by tally-kit before it is written.
- Print shows `Rs.` (the report font has no `₹` glyph).

## Dates

| Kind | GraphQL | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Instant | `DateTime` (ISO string) | `createdAt`, `verifiedAt`, voucher dates |
| Day | `Day` (`"YYYY-MM-DD"`) | Calendar day **in IST** (cash closings, settlement lines, lock dates, GST invoice days) |
| Period | `String` | Settlement month `"2026-09"`; financial year `"2026-27"` |

The financial year runs 1 April to 31 March (IST). Voucher and invoice numbers restart each year
(`MGPL/ARG01/2026-27/000001`: organisation / branch / year / sequence).

## Storage

```mermaid
erDiagram
  ORGANIZATION ||--o{ BRANCH : has
  ORGANIZATION ||--o{ USER : employs
  ORGANIZATION ||--o{ ROLE : defines
  BRANCH ||--o{ PATIENT : registers
  PATIENT ||--o{ BOOKING : books
  BOOKING ||--o{ SAMPLE : yields
  BOOKING ||--o{ REPORT : produces
  BOOKING |o--o| INVOICE : billed_by
  INVOICE ||--o{ PAYMENT : receives
  INVOICE ||--o{ CREDIT_NOTE : reduced_by
  INVOICE ||--o{ VOUCHER : posts
  VOUCHER ||--|{ LEDGER_ENTRY : contains
  LEDGER ||--o{ LEDGER_ENTRY : records
  ACCOUNT_GROUP ||--o{ LEDGER : groups
  CUSTOMER ||--|| LEDGER : owns
  CUSTOMER ||--o{ INVOICE : billed
  PARTNER ||--o{ AGREEMENT : signs
  PARTNER ||--o{ SETTLEMENT : earns
  BRANCH ||--o{ CASH_CLOSING : closes
  BANK_STATEMENT ||--o{ BANK_LINE : lists
  ORGANIZATION ||--o{ PERIOD_LOCK : locks
```

All tables and collections belong to **db-kit**, on PostgreSQL (Sequelize) or MongoDB (Mongoose, replica
set for transactions). Both backends pass the same contract tests, and this API's suite runs on both.
Schema changes are db-kit pull requests, never local tables here.

## GST prerequisites

| Needed for | Set |
|---|---|
| Posting any invoice (place of supply → CGST+SGST or IGST) | The branch's `stateCode` (or its `gstin`) |
| GSTR-1 / GSTR-3B | The organisation's `gstin` (or pass `gstin`) |
| B2B invoices to registered buyers | The customer's `gstin` and `stateCode` |
| Taxable lines | Tax rules (`seedTaxRules`, then confirm each with the CA) |

A branch without a state code fails billing with `BAD_USER_INPUT`. The seed script asks for it.

## Personal data

Patients' names, phones, addresses and results are health data. Do not log request bodies, do not copy
production data into tests (fixtures use fictional names), and keep backups encrypted.


---

## File: docs/11-testing.md

# 11 · Testing

`npm test` runs `test/run.ts`: the real server (Fastify + Yoga) driven over HTTP with `app.inject`, real
auth-kit sessions, and real databases started in-process.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  T["test/run.ts"] --> PG["embedded-postgres<br/>(temp dir)"]
  T --> MG["mongodb-memory-server<br/>replica set"]
  PG & MG --> S["suite(db, tag)"]
  S --> SEED["seed: org APL (GSTIN, branch state 22)<br/>org OTH (tenant isolation)"]
  SEED --> RUN["≈64 checks per backend over POST /graphql"]
  T --> CFG["fromConfig(url): production container path"]
  CFG --> CL["clientSdk: @mgpl-diagnostics/client's session manager"]
  T --> WK["workerSuite: API + BullMQ worker on a real Redis<br/>(REDIS_URL, or redis-server started by the test)"]
```

| Area | What the suite proves |
|---|---|
| Server | `/health` and `{ health }`, introspection off when `INTROSPECTION=0`, depth limit 12 |
| Auth | no token → `UNAUTHENTICATED`, wrong password → `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, login, viewer (null without a token), weak password, reset link through the mailer (unknown emails not revealed), reset ends old sessions, disable signs out at once, `mySessions`, logout |
| Permissions | front desk cannot read the books; registers in branch A, not B; lists show only the viewer's branches; discounts need `invoice:discount`; nested vouchers hidden without `accounts:read` |
| Tenancy | another organisation cannot read the invoice, the patient, or print it; cannot post into its ledgers |
| Catalog | search and price quote without sign-in |
| Lab | patient → booking by catalog code → collect → receive → results with unit, range and flag from the catalog → unverified report does not print → verify, release → booking completed |
| Billing | invoice priced from the catalog, partial payment, overpayment refused, payment → paid with sales and receipt vouchers, qty 0 refused |
| Books | chart setup, trial balance balances, manual voucher, unbalanced voucher refused |
| Finance | tax rules, customer + credit invoice, credit limit, statement, credit note, GSTR-1/3B data with the verify-with-CA list, trial balance CSV with TOTAL row, partner + agreement + settlement preview, lock date → `PERIOD_LOCKED` |
| Documents | booking report PDF and non-header HTML, stored invoice PDF + HTML (totals match), `renderReport` / `invoiceTotals` / `reportTemplates`, bad request → `BAD_USER_INPUT` |
| Tokens | access JWT + refresh token, refresh rotates, spent / unknown refresh token → `INVALID_TOKEN`, edited claims refused, `logout(refreshToken)` ends the session |
| Device binding | login stores the device (`mySessions.deviceId`), same device with a new fingerprint refreshes, another device → `INVALID_TOKEN` and the session ends |
| Jobs | `startDocumentJob` → PDF (in-process), only the owner reads `job(id)`, other organisation → `NOT_FOUND`, missing id → `BAD_USER_INPUT` |
| Worker | jobs go to BullMQ, refresh tokens in Redis, reset link sent by the worker, no reset token in the queue, document rendered by the worker |
| Client SDK | login with device signals, 5 parallel calls on an expiring token → 1 refresh, refresh + retry on `UNAUTHENTICATED`, `session.fetch`, logout |
| Client contract | all client operations valid; every root field covered |
| Performance | 10 invoices with nested `patient` → one batched lookup (no N+1) |

Not covered yet (good next tests): refunds and invoice cancellation, settlement accrue/pay/cancel, cash
closing, bank import and reconciliation, year-end close, P&L / balance sheet values, CORS headers, the
login rate limit.

## Running

```bash
npm test                         # PostgreSQL and MongoDB (first run downloads the binaries)
TEST_BACKENDS=pg npm test        # PostgreSQL only
REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379 npm test   # the worker suite on this Redis (else redis-server is started, or the suite is skipped)
DEBUG=1 TEST_BACKENDS=pg npm test   # print resolver errors
MONGOMS_SYSTEM_BINARY=/usr/bin/mongod npm test   # behind a proxy that blocks the MongoDB download
```

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job id `ci`, required on `main`) runs `npm run kits`, typecheck, the tests
on both backends, the build, and checks that `schema.graphql`, `docs/04-api-reference.md` and
`llms-full.txt` are current.

## The client contract

`kits.json` pins `@mgpl-diagnostics/client`. The `[static]` checks validate every GraphQL operation the
client sends (141) against `buildSchema()` and check that each query and mutation has one, so a renamed
or new field fails here before it reaches an app. Change the client first, then bump its ref.

## Adding a test

Add checks to `suite()` in `test/run.ts` with `ok(condition, "[tag] what it proves")`. Use the `gql(token,
query, variables)` helper and the seeded tokens (`owner`, `desk`, …). Keep fixtures fictional.

## File: docs/12-deployment.md

# 12 · Deployment

## Shape

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U["Browsers / apps"] -- HTTPS --> LB["Load balancer / reverse proxy<br/>TLS, gzip"]
  LB -- "/graphql, /health" --> A1["api #1"]
  LB --> A2["api #2"]
  A1 & A2 --> DB[("PostgreSQL<br/>or MongoDB replica set")]
  A1 & A2 --> R[("Redis<br/>sessions · queues")]
  R --> W1["worker #1"]
  R --> W2["worker #2"]
  W1 & W2 --> DB
  W1 & W2 -- "mail-kit (SMTP_URL)" --> MAIL["mail server"]
  A1 & A2 -. reads .-> SIG["signature files<br/>(secret volume)"]
  W1 & W2 -. reads .-> SIG
```

- **One server** can run without Redis (sessions in memory, lost on restart; jobs run in the API process).
- **Two or more servers need Redis**: sessions, refresh tokens and login limits must be shared.
- **Workers** (`node dist/worker.js`) need Redis and the same environment as the API (database,
  `JWT_SECRET`, signature files). Run one or more; see [16-worker.md](16-worker.md).
- The process is stateless otherwise; scale horizontally.

## Build and run

```bash
npm run kits          # or `npm ci` once every kit is on the registry
npm run build         # dist/main.js, dist/worker.js
NODE_ENV=production node dist/main.js     # API
NODE_ENV=production node dist/worker.js   # worker (with REDIS_URL)
```

A container image: Node 22 slim, copy `dist/`, `node_modules/` and `package.json`, run
`node dist/main.js`, expose `PORT`. The PDF engine needs no system fonts (fonts are bundled), but
report-kit's resvg is a native module: build the image on the same platform it runs on.

## Production checklist

| | Item |
|---|---|
| ☐ | `NODE_ENV=production`, `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL` set from secrets |
| ☐ | `JWT_SECRET` set from secrets (≥ 32 random characters, e.g. `openssl rand -base64 48`), the same on every API server |
| ☐ | At least one worker running (`node dist/worker.js`) with `SMTP_URL` and `MAIL_FROM` set |
| ☐ | `CORS_ORIGINS` lists exactly the app origins (no `*`) |
| ☐ | `GRAPHIQL` and `INTROSPECTION` off (the defaults in production) |
| ☐ | `TRUST_PROXY=true` behind one load balancer, `TRUST_PROXY=2` behind a CDN plus a load balancer (login limits use the client IP) |
| ☐ | `MGPL_SAMPLES` off (the default in production) |
| ☐ | Signature files mounted read-only; `MGPL_SIGNATURE_*_FILE` point at them |
| ☐ | `PASSWORD_RESET_URL` points at the app's reset page, and a mailer is wired (below) |
| ☐ | First organisation seeded (`npm run seed`) with the branch `stateCode` and the org GSTIN |
| ☐ | Tax rules seeded **and confirmed by the CA** (`verifyWithCA`) |
| ☐ | Database backups (point-in-time for Postgres), encrypted |
| ☐ | Health check on `GET /health` (200 `{ ok: true }`, 503 when the database is down) |
| ☐ | Logs shipped; request bodies are not logged (they hold patient data) |

## Sending password-reset emails

Set `SMTP_URL` and `MAIL_FROM`. The worker (or the API, without Redis) sends the mail with
[mail-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/mail-kit): the "password-reset" mail is written in its mail
design language and goes out as HTML plus plain text, in the lab's brand (name, address, phone from
report-kit's lab profile). Any SMTP provider works (Gmail or Zoho app passwords, Amazon SES, Brevo);
mail-kit refuses to send without TLS to a remote server. The provider's SPF and DKIM records must cover
the domain in `MAIL_FROM`.

Without `SMTP_URL`, `MAIL_WEBHOOK_URL` still works: the worker POSTs `{ to, subject, text }` JSON to it.
With neither, reset links are not sent (the API still answers `true`). To send another way, embed with your own `Mailer`, in the
worker's process when you run workers:

```ts
import { buildServer, createContainer, loadConfig, type Mailer } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/api";

const mailer: Mailer = {
  async passwordReset(to, link, expiresAt) {
    await sendEmail({ to: to.email, subject: "Reset your password", text: `Hi ${to.name}, ${link} (until ${expiresAt.toISOString()})` });
  },
};
const container = await createContainer({ config: loadConfig(), mailer });
await (await buildServer(container)).listen({ port: container.config.port, host: container.config.host });
```

## Database operations

- **PostgreSQL**: `createDb` creates missing tables on start (`sequelize.sync()`, which never alters
  existing ones). Take a backup before upgrading db-kit and apply any migration its changelog lists.
- **MongoDB**: must be a replica set (transactions). `createDb` syncs indexes on start (`syncIndexes`).
- **Redis**: sessions, refresh tokens and queued jobs. Losing it signs everyone out and drops queued
  jobs; turn on AOF persistence if queued emails must survive a Redis restart.

## Upgrading kits

Bump the version in `package.json` (and the ref in `kits.json` while CI builds from source), run
`npm test` on both backends, regenerate `schema.graphql` if types changed, deploy. tally-kit changes of
behaviour are versioned decisions; read its changelog.


---

## File: docs/13-adding-a-feature.md

# 13 · Adding a feature

Every feature walks the same layers. Example: **a query `patientInvoicesDue(patientId)`**.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["1 · Kit<br/>(if new logic or storage)"] --> B["2 · Service<br/>src/services"]
  B --> C["3 · Schema<br/>src/schema/*.graphql.ts"]
  C --> D["4 · Controller<br/>src/controllers"]
  D --> E["5 · Test<br/>test/run.ts"]
  E --> F["6 · Generated files<br/>schema · reference · llms"]
  F --> G["7 · Client<br/>operations · types · method"]
```

## 1. Does it belong in a kit?

| The change is… | Where |
|---|---|
| A new table, column or repository method | **db-kit** PR (both `mongo/` and `pg/`, contract tests) |
| A domain rule (GST, settlements, credit limits) | **finance-kit** |
| Posting or books reports | **tally-kit** |
| A permission | **auth-kit** `PERMISSIONS` + the right `SYSTEM_ROLES` |
| A test, range or price | **catalog-kit** `data/catalog.json` |
| A print layout | **report-kit** / **invoice-kit** |
| Wiring, authorisation, mapping to GraphQL | here |

## 2. Service

```ts
// src/services/billing.service.ts
async dueForPatient(actor: Actor, patientId: Id, scope: "all" | Id[]) {
  mustOwn(await this.repos.patients.get(patientId), actor.orgId, "Patient", patientId);
  const invoices = await scopedFind(this.repos.invoices, { patientId }, scope, 200, 0, "createdAt");
  return invoices.filter((i) => i.duePaise > 0 && i.status !== "cancelled");
}
```

Services take `(actor, …)`, check ownership, use the kits, and never import GraphQL.

## 3. Schema

```ts
// src/schema/billing.graphql.ts
extend type Query {
  """Unpaid invoices of one patient, newest first."""
  patientInvoicesDue(patientId: ID!): [Invoice!]!
}
```

## 4. Controller

```ts
// src/controllers/billing.controller.ts, inside Query
patientInvoicesDue: (_: unknown, a: { patientId: string }, ctx: Ctx) =>
  ctx.services.billing.dueForPatient(actorOf(ctx), a.patientId, branchScope(ctx, "invoice:read")),
```

Always: `authorize` / `branchScope` first, ids checked against the organisation, `cap()` on limits.
Controllers are wrapped in `withErrorCodes`, so domain errors get codes automatically.

## 5. Test

```ts
const due = await gql(desk, `query($p: ID!) { patientInvoicesDue(patientId: $p) { invoiceNo duePaise } }`, { p: patientId });
ok(due.data?.patientInvoicesDue.length === 1, `[${tag}] patientInvoicesDue lists the unpaid invoice`);
```

Add a negative check too (another organisation, or a user without the permission).

## 6. Generated files

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm test
npm run schema && npm run docs:reference && npm run llms
```

Update the hand-written docs that describe the area (flows, errors) and add an example to `docs/examples/`.

## 7. Client

In `mgpl-diagnostics/client`: add the operation to `src/graphql/operations.ts`, the result type to
`src/graphql/types.ts`, a method to `src/graphql/client.ts`, a row to `docs/graphql.md`; release; then bump
the client ref here so the contract test covers it.

## Checklist

- [ ] Permission exists in auth-kit and the right roles grant it
- [ ] No `orgId` or `actorId` arguments
- [ ] Money in paise, days as `Day`
- [ ] Multi-record writes inside a kit transaction
- [ ] Nested fields through loaders
- [ ] Positive and negative tests on both backends
- [ ] schema.graphql, 04-api-reference.md, llms-full.txt regenerated

## File: docs/14-client.md

# 14 · Client

Frontends use [`@mgpl-diagnostics/client`](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/client) (zero dependencies).
Its `createMgplGraphQLClient` has one typed method per operation of this API.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph App["Your app (any framework)"]
    UI["UI + state"] --> SDK["createMgplGraphQLClient()"]
  end
  SDK -- "POST /graphql" --> API["api"]
  SDK -. "documentBlob / csvBlob" .-> DL["download · open · print"]
```

```ts
import { createMgplGraphQLClient, createSessionManager, webSessionStorage, documentBlob, printBlob } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/client";

const session = createSessionManager({ url: import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL + "/graphql", storage: webSessionStorage() });
const mgpl = createMgplGraphQLClient({ url: import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL + "/graphql", session });

await mgpl.auth.login({ email, password, orgCode: "MGPL" });   // device signals added; tokens kept and refreshed
const me = await mgpl.auth.viewer();
const canBill = await mgpl.auth.can("invoice:create", branchId);

const hits = await mgpl.catalog.search("lft");
const { booking } = await mgpl.bookings.create({ branchId, patientId, tests: hits.slice(0, 1).map((h) => ({ testCode: h.test.code! })) });
const doc = await mgpl.documents.bookingReports(booking.id, { variant: "non_header" });
printBlob(documentBlob(doc));
```

| Need | Method |
|---|---|
| Sign in / out, sessions | `auth.login`, `auth.logout`, `auth.refresh` (automatic), `auth.sessions`, `auth.changePassword` |
| Session state in any UI library | `mgpl.session.subscribe` / `getSnapshot` / `store`, `useMgplSession` (React) |
| TanStack Query, SWR | `mgplQuery`, `mgplMutation`, `mgplKey`, `mgplFetcher`, `clearOnSignOut` |
| Background documents | `documents.startJob`, `documents.waitForJob` |
| Show or hide UI by permission | `auth.viewer().permissions`, `auth.can(permission, branchId)` |
| Result-entry form | `catalog.test(code, sex)` (parameters, units, ranges) or `documents.templates()` |
| Live preview | `documents.renderReport(request, { format: "html" })` |
| Desk | `patients.*`, `bookings.*`, `samples.*`, `invoices.*` |
| Pathologist | `reports.saveResults`, `reports.verify`, `reports.release` |
| Accounts | `books.*`, `gst.*`, `receivables.*`, `settlements.*`, `cash.*`, `bank.*`, `periods.*`, `exports.*` |
| Anything custom | `request(query, variables)` |

Errors arrive as `MgplGraphQLError` with `code` ([05-errors.md](05-errors.md)). The full method list is in
the client's `docs/graphql.md`.

## Sessions with any library

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph App["Your app"]
    UI["React · Vue · Svelte · Solid · RN"] -- "subscribe / getSnapshot" --> SM["session manager"]
    DATA["TanStack Query · SWR"] -- "mgplQuery / mgplFetcher" --> SDK["GraphQL client"]
    OTHER["Apollo · urql · graphql-request"] -- "fetch: session.fetch" --> SM
    SDK --> SM
  end
  SM -- "Bearer access token · refreshSession (single flight, Web Locks) · device signals" --> API["api"]
```

The client's [docs/session.md](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/client/blob/main/docs/session.md)
has the details: storages, cross-tab refresh, device signals and what they contain.

## Without the SDK

Any GraphQL client works. Send `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` and
`content-type: application/json` to `POST /graphql`. When a request returns `UNAUTHENTICATED`, call
`refreshSession(refreshToken, device)` once and retry; on `INVALID_TOKEN`, sign in again. The schema is
in [schema.graphql](../schema.graphql) for code generators; introspection is off in production.

## File: docs/15-glossary.md

# 15 · Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Booking** | A patient's order for one or more tests on one visit |
| **Sample** | A specimen (blood, urine, …) collected for a booking, with a barcode; one per sample type |
| **Report** | The results of one test for a booking; goes draft → entered → verified → released |
| **Template** | report-kit's layout for a test (rows, units, ranges); results keyed by field |
| **Profile** | A group of tests sold together (e.g. LFT, KFT) |
| **UHID** | Unique health ID: the lab's patient number |
| **MRP** | Maximum retail price of a test, in rupees, from the catalog |
| **Paise** | 1/100 of a rupee; every amount in the API is integer paise |
| **Branch** | A lab or collection centre of the organisation; holds its own stock of patients, bookings, cash |
| **Header / non-header** | Print with the letterhead, or without it for pre-printed stationery |
| **Voucher** | A double-entry accounting document: sales, receipt, payment, journal, contra, credit note, … |
| **Ledger** | An account (Cash, Bank, Sales, a customer, a partner) inside an account group |
| **Trial balance** | Every ledger's debit/credit balance; totals must be equal |
| **Day book** | All vouchers of a period |
| **Lock date** | No posting on or before it (period closed) |
| **Financial year (FY)** | 1 April – 31 March, written `2026-27` |
| **GSTIN** | 15-character GST registration number; its first two digits are the state code |
| **State code** | GST code of a state (22 = Chhattisgarh); decides CGST+SGST (same state) vs IGST |
| **Place of supply** | The state where the service is supplied, for GST |
| **HSN / SAC** | Classification codes for goods / services on invoices |
| **GSTR-1 / GSTR-3B** | Monthly GST returns: outward supplies detail / summary with tax payable |
| **B2B / B2C / B2CL / B2CS** | Supplies to registered businesses / consumers (large / small) |
| **CDNR / CDNUR** | Credit and debit notes to registered / unregistered buyers |
| **Credit note** | Reduces an issued invoice (with its tax); our "partial cancel" |
| **Receivable** | Money owed by B2B customers (hospitals, insurers, TPAs, corporates) |
| **Ageing** | Open amounts by how overdue they are (0–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+ days) |
| **Partner** | A collection centre or franchise that earns a share of billing |
| **Settlement** | A month's partner share: preview → draft → accrued → paid |
| **TDS** | Tax deducted at source on payments to partners (section and rate are CA-confirmed config) |
| **bp (basis points)** | 1/100 of a percent: 2500 bp = 25 % |
| **MDR** | Merchant discount rate: the card/UPI fee the bank deducts from settlements |
| **BRS** | Bank reconciliation statement: book balance vs bank balance and the items between |
| **Verify with CA** | Values (rates, thresholds, sections) the lab's chartered accountant must confirm |
| **Kit** | One of our libraries (auth, db, catalog, report, invoice, tally, finance) used inside the API |
| **Actor** | `{ userId, orgId }` of the signed-in user, from the session |
